Atrophy

AT-ruh-fee -- three syllables, stress on the first syllable, AT. · verb

Hear It

What It Means

To atrophy is to waste away or gradually decline.

The doctor warned that the muscles around Theo's knee would atrophy unless he did his physical-therapy exercises every day.

Worked Example

Maya was the chess club's sharpest tactician before she quit for three years. On her first night back, she stares at a position she once would have solved in seconds -- and sees nothing. The patterns that used to leap out at her are simply gone.

Maya's tactical skill has atrophied: wasted away from lack of use. Atrophy began as a medical word -- muscles shrinking when nothing makes them work -- and extends naturally to skills and abilities. The key idea is always disuse: what you do not exercise, you slowly lose.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

weaken: to lose strength

deteriorate: to grow steadily worse

degenerate: to decline into a worse condition

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

strengthen: to make or grow stronger

flourish: to grow vigorously and well

Where it sits · how hard the loss is to reverse — weaken → atrophy → degenerate

weaken vs. atrophy: Weaken says only that strength is dropping, from any cause, while atrophy names the slow, wasting kind of loss that comes specifically from disuse and neglect.

degenerate vs. atrophy: Degenerate is the strongest and grimmest: an atrophied muscle has shrunk from idleness and can often be rebuilt, but tissue that degenerates is breaking down into something worse.

Build the Word

The pieces

prefix — a-

prefix — a-: without, lacking (Greek)

root — troph-

root — troph-: nourishment, food (Greek trophe)

suffix — -y

suffix — -y: noun-forming ending (state, condition) (Greek (-ia))

Put it together

Put it together: Greek a- ('without') plus trophe ('nourishment') plus the noun ending -y names the state of going unfed. A muscle -- or a language, or a talent -- that atrophies is wasting away from lack of use.

Use the root in a new word: dystrophy

Use the root in a new word: dystrophy: Muscular dystrophy is literally 'bad nourishment': the same feeding root, but here the muscles waste because the body cannot keep them fed.

Root Check

Word Choice

Atrophy is about wasting from disuse: muscles atrophy in a cast, skills atrophy without practice. Keep it apart from its three unit-mates: wither means to dry up and shrivel (a plant, or figuratively hopes and confidence); ebb is a tide-like receding that may flow back; taper is a gradual reduction toward an end point. Only atrophy blames idleness for the loss.
